Scope: HOPE-R is an independently proposed reference design tested on deterministic fixtures, not author code or a benchmark result.

:::

The most useful criticism ends with a runnable alternative.

Parts 1 through 11 found a valuable local idea inside HOPE v1: a neuron can be
treated as a complete function-valued operator, not merely as an incoming
filter. They also found that the published pipeline asks several incompatible
objects to carry that idea. Pair-local surrogates are assembled as though they
came from one distribution. A symbolic merge target is not always the
physical one-parent map that Algorithm 2 executes. Local cache refresh omits
graph dependencies. DEFT freezes destinations while the complete operator is
owned by its source. The experiments do not resolve those specification gaps.

Part 12 builds forward from that record.

HOPE-R is a framework-independent proposed reference design with four joined
contracts:

1. Every neuron in one layer is evaluated under one declared weighted
   calibration measure.
2. A physical merge fits one realizable parent to the executed child sum and
   reports the residual it actually leaves.
3. Every physical channel mutation has an explicit graph dependency closure,
   live resource account, and fail-closed block boundary.
4. Transfer uses fixed-width slots, complete source-owned masks, explicit
   optimizer state, and task-declared BatchNorm and evaluation state.

These are proposed repairs, not an author implementation and not results
reported by HOPE v1. The supporting audit uses deterministic float64 fixtures.
It trains no model, reads no benchmark dataset, and makes no claim about
accuracy, convergence, latency, or how often a local failure occurs in a
trained network.

## Correction begins by separating the branches

A corrected method cannot quietly replace a paper equation and then continue
calling the result a reproduction. HOPE-R therefore preserves three distinct
labels:

| Branch | Meaning | Permitted conclusion |
|---|---|---|
| Paper-literal | The equation or algorithm as printed in HOPE v1 | What the paper specifies on the declared input |
| Deterministic fixture | A finite NumPy construction used to test one boundary | What happens on that fixture within enforced tolerances |
| Proposed HOPE-R repair | A new rule chosen after the audit | What the implemented rule guarantees in its declared domain |

The separation is visible in code. Paper-literal modules remain under
`hope_repro.paper_literal`. The new modules live under
`hope_repro.proposed_repairs.hope_r`. The Part 12 audit imports the latter as
proposed repairs and retains paper-literal calculations only as named
comparisons or negative controls.

This distinction prevents four common overclaims:

- calibrated exactness is not population exactness;
- a positive-semidefinite fixture Gram is not proof that the paper's
  pair-assembled Gram is always positive semidefinite;
- an exact-twin merge is not universal one-neuron preservation;
- a zero-drift optimizer fixture is not evidence of benchmark retention.

The purpose of HOPE-R is narrower: make the desired invariants explicit enough
that an implementation can either satisfy them or fail before changing a
model.

## The exact paper anchors stay attached

The corrected pipeline answers specific parts of the authenticated HOPE v1
paper. It does not replace their provenance. The Part 12 source map uses these
exact anchors from `paper/equation-map.json`:

| HOPE-R boundary | Exact paper anchor used for comparison |
|---|---|
| Functional atom and kernels | Eqs. 1-5, PDF pages 5-9 |
| Printed physical merge | Eq. 6 and Eqs. 7-18, PDF pages 13-16 |
| Residual eviction | Eqs. 19-20, PDF page 17 |
| Planning and payoff | Eqs. 21-23, PDF pages 18-19 |
| DEFT partition and routing | Eqs. 24-29, PDF pages 21-23 |
| Common expectation geometry | Eq. 30 and Proposition A.1, PDF page 35 |
| Cached payoff and pair geometry | Appendix B.2-B.4 and Eqs. 36-40, PDF pages 38-40 |
| Self and cross-kernel comparison branches | Eqs. 73-85, PDF pages 52-56 |
| Executed aggregate map | Eq. 86, PDF page 57 |
| Identity-shortcut assumptions | Eqs. 93-97, PDF page 58 |
| Core ownership and released vessels | Definition H.1 and Eqs. 102-118, PDF pages 62-67 |
| Physical surgery, compression, and transfer | Algorithms 1-3, PDF pages 68-70 |

The anchors matter because HOPE-R changes different things for different
reasons. It retains Eq. 30's common-expectation logic, but changes how the
measure is obtained. It retains Eq. 86's sum-map target, but changes how a
realizable physical parent is selected. It retains the useful routing idea of
Eqs. 28-29, but changes parameter ownership and slot lifecycle.

`source_map.csv` is the canonical machine-readable route from each Part 12
claim to these paper locations and to the independent implementation branch.

## One layer gets one declared calibration measure

The first repair resolves the geometry mismatch from Parts 3 through 5.

Let a layer receive declared calibration rows

$$
x_1,\ldots,x_m
$$

with nonnegative weights

$$
q_1,\ldots,q_m,
\qquad
\sum_{n=1}^{m}q_n=1.
$$

For neuron $i$, fold its inference-time affine state and evaluate

$$
a_i(x_n)=\operatorname{ReLU}(w_i^\top x_n+b_i).
$$

The calibrated cross-moment is then

$$
K_{ij}^{\mathrm{cal}}
=
\sum_{n=1}^{m}q_n a_i(x_n)a_j(x_n).
$$

Every entry uses the same rows and the same normalized weights. No pair may
silently choose a new covariance, a new marginal law, or a new sample subset.
The label attached to the calibration measure is carried into downstream
merge results.

proposed_repair (P12-CALIBRATED-COMMON-MEASURE): HOPE-R evaluates all neurons
in one layer under one declared weighted calibration measure, so the exact
activation moments share one distribution.

The word calibrated is an essential limitation. This mode consumes input
rows. It is not strictly data-free, even when the rows are unlabeled. A user
must declare their source, weighting, preprocessing, and sampling policy. A
different calibration measure defines a different geometry.

This is preferable to preserving a data-free label by hiding incompatible
pairwise laws. It also creates an experimental obligation: a future trained
study must test calibration-source and calibration-size sensitivity rather
than treating the selected rows as an invisible constant.

## The common Gram is positive semidefinite by construction

Collect the calibrated activations in a matrix

$$
A_{n,i}=a_i(x_n)
$$

and let $D=\operatorname{diag}(q_1,\ldots,q_m)$. The whole-layer Gram is

$$
G=A^\top D A
=
(D^{1/2}A)^\top(D^{1/2}A).
$$

For any vector $c$,

$$
c^\top Gc
=
\lVert D^{1/2}Ac\rVert_2^2
\ge 0.
$$

This is the shared-distribution guarantee anticipated by Eq. 30 and
Proposition A.1 on PDF page 35. It does not need separately warped pairwise
correlations to happen to assemble into one feasible matrix.

The implementation still validates the output. It checks finite values,
symmetry, and the smallest eigenvalue against a declared float64 roundoff
tolerance. Material asymmetry or negative curvature raises an error. Small
accepted numerical negativity remains visible in the returned certificate
rather than being silently projected away.

verified_fact (P12-COMMON-GRAM-PSD): on the declared Part 12 weighted
calibration fixtures, the exact activation table produces a
positive-semidefinite Gram by construction and the fail-closed spectral check
finds no material negative eigenvalue.

The result is local in two ways. It concerns the declared activation rows, and
it concerns the Part 12 fixtures. It is not a claim that arbitrary empirical
calibration represents the target population, nor that the paper-literal
pair construction has acquired this property retroactively.

The diagonal of this common Gram supplies each calibrated self-moment. HOPE-R
then computes the functional capacity of neuron $i$ as

$$
\sqrt{G_{ii}}\,\lVert v_i\rVert_2,
$$

where $v_i$ is the complete outgoing vector. Positive rescaling of the
incoming affine coordinates with reciprocal outgoing rescaling leaves the
represented contribution and the tested capacity unchanged.

## BatchNorm and kernel limits are explicit

Equation 1 on PDF page 5 motivates folding BatchNorm into the functional
affine map. HOPE-R performs that fold with the supplied finite epsilon intact.
For raw affine state $w_0,b_0$, BatchNorm scale $\gamma$, shift $\beta$,
running mean $\mu$, running variance $\sigma^2$, and epsilon $\epsilon$,
the folded values are

$$
s=\frac{\gamma}{\sqrt{\sigma^2+\epsilon}},
\qquad
w=sw_0,
\qquad
b=\beta+s(b_0-\mu).
$$

The denominator must be strictly positive. Negative variance, negative
epsilon, non-finite input, and non-finite output fail closed.

The zero-scale boundary is handled before unsafe multiplication. If
$\gamma=0$, the folded affine map is the deterministic constant $\beta$,
even when an irrelevant raw subtraction would overflow. The corresponding
zero-variance ReLU self-moment is exactly

$$
\operatorname{ReLU}(\beta)^2.
$$

It is not replaced by a tiny positive variance and it is not sent through a
formula whose derivation assumes positive scale.

HOPE-R also keeps two cross-kernel APIs separate:

- `calibrated_cross_kernel` is exact with respect to the declared weighted
  empirical measure;
- `zero_bias_cross_kernel_approximation` is explicitly the zero-bias angular
  comparison associated with Eqs. 84-85 on PDF page 56.

The exact biased pair moment in Eqs. 80-83 on PDF pages 54-55 remains a
paper-literal comparison branch. It is not used to smuggle pair-specific
surrogates into the common calibrated Gram.

proposed_repair (P12-KERNEL-BOUNDARY-CONTRACT): HOPE-R folds finite-epsilon
BatchNorm explicitly, implements the deterministic zero-scale ReLU limit, and
keeps calibrated exact cross-moments separate from the paper-literal
zero-bias approximation.

`common_gram_cases.csv` records the deterministic Gram, scale-symmetry, fold,
and boundary cases. Those rows establish API behavior, not a population model
and not a benchmark result.

## The physical merge target is the executed child sum

Equation 86 on PDF page 57 defines the aggregate tuple map as a sum of
functional contributions. If two child neurons contribute vector-valued maps
$f_i$ and $f_j$, the object that one retained physical vessel must replace
is

$$
F(x)=f_i(x)+f_j(x).
$$

That target is different from preserving two duplicated parent coordinates in
an abstract comparison space. Algorithm 2 on PDF page 69 retains one child
vessel and purges the other. The realized post-surgery network therefore has
one scalar ReLU activation and one outgoing vector where it previously had
two.

HOPE-R scores that actual one-parent problem. For every calibration row it
forms the child sum $F(x_n)$. A candidate parent has augmented affine
direction $d=[w;b]$, activation

$$
h_d(x_n)=\operatorname{ReLU}(d^\top[x_n;1]),
$$

and outgoing vector $v$. For fixed $d$, it solves the weighted
least-squares problem

$$
v_d^*
=
\arg\min_v
\sum_n q_n
\lVert F(x_n)-h_d(x_n)v\rVert_2^2.
$$

The denominator-zero case has an explicit zero-output solution. Otherwise the
outgoing vector is the closed-form weighted least-squares fit. The returned
record includes the selected direction, fitted outgoing vector, child-sum
norm, realized parent norm, absolute residual, relative residual, candidate
count, span rank, and calibration-measure label.

The incoming search is deterministic and realizable. It stays within the at
most two-dimensional augmented affine span of the children. It always includes
the signed child directions as anchors. A rank-two case adds a fixed
full-circle angular candidate set. HOPE-R selects the smallest measured
residual among that declared finite set.

proposed_repair (P12-SUM-MAP-MERGE): HOPE-R ranks a physical one-parent merge
by its measured residual against the executed child sum and searches a
deterministic realizable direction set.

This is why the method is named `sum_map_optimized`, not universally
sum-preserving. The optimization is exact in the outgoing vector for each
candidate and deterministic over the candidate set. It is not a proof of a
global optimum over every possible ReLU parent, and it does not say that an
arbitrary non-twin pair has a zero-residual one-neuron representation.

## Exact twins receive an anchor, not a universal theorem

Exact twins are the realizable boundary a corrected merge should not miss.
Two positively rescaled parameterizations can describe the same functional
contribution because ReLU is positively homogeneous. Their augmented
directions are collinear, and a retained child direction is already present in
the candidate set.

On the declared zero-bias and biased exact-twin fixtures, the fitted outgoing
vector doubles the realized anchored contribution. The one retained parent
therefore matches the two-child sum within the enforced numerical tolerance.
The same fixture remains invariant when the child parameterizations are
changed by positive incoming scaling and reciprocal outgoing scaling.

verified_fact (P12-TWIN-PRESERVATION): on the declared exact-twin fixtures,
the corrected physical merge retains an anchored child direction, doubles its
realized contribution through the fitted outgoing vector, and matches the
original child sum to numerical tolerance.

The non-twin control is equally important. A noncollinear pair returns a
measured residual rather than being relabeled as exact. That residual is
evaluated under the same calibration measure as the candidate fit. A zero
value would certify equality only on those declared rows; a nonzero value is a
direct local record of what the physical merge failed to preserve.

`merge_cases.csv` preserves both boundaries. It does not license a claim of
universal non-twin preservation, final-logit control, or downstream loss
control.

## Physical surgery invalidates a graph closure

Algorithms 1 and 2 on PDF pages 68-69 mutate physical channels. Once a channel
is removed or two children are replaced, the change is not confined to one
cached pair in one layer.

HOPE-R requires a complete explicit graph declaration before surgery. Every
physical channel has a stable `ChannelRef`. Every live input coordinate names
its source. Every producer names every direct consumer, including fan-out
branches. A terminal channel may have no consumer; an unresolved nonterminal
channel may not masquerade as one.

For a declared prune or merge, the dependency plan includes:

- every changed-layer capacity, outgoing, incoming, BatchNorm-assumption, and
  affected pair key, including removed children and the retained merge-parent
  vessel;
- every resolved predecessor outgoing dependency;
- every affected predecessor capacity and pair dependency;
- every resolved successor incoming and capacity dependency;
- every successor pair and BatchNorm assumption;
- every residual-block score spanning an affected layer.

The plan is constructed before physical mutation and serialized in canonical
order. A merge must explicitly name which child vessel receives the synthesized
parent; both child records are invalidated, the removed child is discarded, and
the retained vessel is recomputed. Stable channel IDs are identity tokens, not
a promise that surviving channels will be renumbered densely.

proposed_repair (P12-DEPENDENCY-CLOSURE): after physical channel surgery,
HOPE-R invalidates the changed layer, all resolved predecessor and successor
dependencies, every affected successor BatchNorm assumption, and every
spanning block score.

This is a deliberately fail-closed contract. Grouped and depthwise
convolution, shared parameters, unknown operators, incomplete consumer maps,
and unresolved fan-out are rejected. The reference module does not claim to
trace a framework model automatically. A caller must supply and validate the
graph it wants to mutate.

The deterministic branched fixture now constructs its oracle independently of
the invalidation plan. `cache_universe(graph)` enumerates 37 pre-surgery cache
records from the declared graph. A separate topology surgery produces the
32-record post-prune graph, and graph-derived structural digests identify 25
removed or changed prune keys. The merge oracle independently identifies 29
keys because it also refreshes the retained physical parent. Both plan key sets
match their oracles exactly, with zero missing and zero extra keys.

The refresh comparison starts from the complete pre-surgery snapshot, removes
the plan's invalidated keys, recomputes surviving affected keys from the
post-surgery graph, and compares the resulting dictionary with the independently
built post-surgery snapshot. A changed-layer-only negative control leaves 20
dependent records stale.

verified_fact (P12-REFRESH-EQUIVALENCE): on the declared abstract branched
fixture, dependency-aware structural refresh agrees with the independently
enumerated post-surgery cache snapshot, while the deliberately local negative
control does not. This is a structural cache-contract test, not a numerical
capacity or framework-runtime equivalence claim.

`invalidation_cases.csv` records the resolved branch, closure categories,
refresh comparison, and fail-closed cases. This fixture is not evidence that
an undeclared production graph has been traced completely.

## Resource accounting names the unit before counting it

Section 10 and Appendix B.4 distinguish constant scalar arithmetic for one
cached candidate from the scan needed to choose among live candidates. HOPE-R
keeps those units separate.

At every declared state, the resource record can report:

- live widths;
- live prune, merge, and eligible-block candidates;
- exhaustive candidate evaluations in the current scan;
- the full declared sequence of trajectory scan states;
- pair-cache entries and their scalar and index payload bytes;
- canonical key-record bytes, separately excluding container overhead;
- dependency-plan refresh evaluations and unique refreshed keys;
- calibration examples, input values, output elements, and branch-cost
  evaluations.

Immediate physical payoff is also recomputed from the live graph. Removing a
channel counts its generating weights, optional bias, declared BatchNorm
values, and the corresponding input coordinate in every explicit downstream
consumer. Fan-out is counted branch by branch. The paper's initial static
parameter payoff remains available as a separate baseline; it is not silently
substituted for the live release after prior surgery.

proposed_repair (P12-LIVE-RESOURCE-ACCOUNTING): HOPE-R records initialization,
live candidates, exhaustive scans, trajectory evaluations, cache storage,
dependency refreshes, calibration evaluations, and immediate live physical
payoff without converting those counts into a wall-clock claim.

The count record is not a benchmark. It does not include Python container
overhead unless explicitly added, allocator behavior, kernel fusion, device
traffic, parallel scheduling, or elapsed time. It also does not turn parameter
count into FLOPs or latency. Those require separately instrumented
measurements.

`resource_accounting.csv` is the canonical count record. It keeps the initial
static comparator and live physical values in different fields.

## Residual-block handling has a narrow eligibility gate

The paper's Eqs. 19-20 on PDF page 17 sum local internal-layer quantities and
normalize by an identity-path capacity. Parts 6 and 8 showed why that
construction does not automatically become a function-level bound for a
sequential nonlinear residual branch.

HOPE-R does not generalize the claim. It accepts only a declared:

- ResNet V1 block;
- post-activation boundary;
- identity shortcut;
- unit stride;
- equal input and output shape.

For that eligible boundary, the calibrated repair directly compares the
retained output

$$
\operatorname{ReLU}(x+F(x))
$$

with the evicted output

$$
\operatorname{ReLU}(x)
$$

on declared calibration arrays. The score is the weighted mean squared
boundary displacement. It measures the executed block change rather than
summing local sequential proxies.

Projection shortcuts, stride changes, ResNet V2 ordering, missing skips,
shape changes, and unresolved cases are rejected with explicit reason codes.
Eqs. 93-97 on PDF page 58 remain the exact identity-shortcut comparison
anchor; they are not treated as authority for unsupported block families.

proposed_repair (P12-BLOCK-ELIGIBILITY): HOPE-R accepts only resolved
same-shape stride-one post-activation ResNet V1 identity shortcuts for this
calibrated direct branch score and fails closed outside that domain.

`block_eligibility.csv` records the accepted boundary and each named rejection.
It does not show how often any block type occurs in a benchmark architecture,
nor whether evicting an eligible block preserves accuracy.

## DEFT keeps stable physical slots

The Part 10 audit found three distinct partition procedures across Eqs. 24-27,
Definition H.1, and Algorithm 3. HOPE-R chooses one instead of trying to prove
all three equivalent.

For each layer, the caller declares a fixed ordered tuple of stable slot IDs
and an integer core count $k_\ell$. HOPE-R ranks current functional capacity
within that layer by:

1. capacity descending;
2. stable slot ID ascending for an exact tie.

Exactly $k_\ell$ slots become core. The remaining active slots become slack.
The core count, tie rule, capacities, ranked IDs, and final assignment are
returned together. Mapping insertion order and physical array order do not
silently resolve ties.

The slot lifecycle has four explicit states:

| State | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `core` | Source-owned complete operator protected from target updates |
| `slack` | Active plastic slot |
| `released` | Fixed physical position retained but inactive and not trainable |
| `reinitialized` | Reused position with a live incoming path and initially silent outgoing path |

A slack slot may be released without changing tensor width or stable identity.
Core slots have no release transition after the partition and remain
protected. Only a released slot may be reinitialized. A reinitialized slot may
then enter ordinary slack, or be released again. Direct transitions that would
create a reinitialized state without parameters are rejected.

Reinitialization is asymmetric on purpose. The deterministic initializer gives
the slot a nonzero, normalized incoming vector, affine scale one, affine shift
zero, and an all-zero outgoing vector. On the declared all-ones probe, the
incoming ReLU activation is live while the initial vector contribution is
exactly zero.

That creates a two-stage gradient path in the scalar squared-loss fixture. On
the first backward pass, the outgoing parameter receives a nonzero gradient
while the internal parameters remain blocked by the zero outgoing value. After
the first outgoing update, the second backward pass reaches the incoming and
affine parameters. The fixture demonstrates local gradient liveness; it does
not prove convergence or useful feature learning.

proposed_repair (P12-FIXED-WIDTH-DEFT): HOPE-R uses stable fixed-width slots,
one explicit layer-wise top-k current-capacity partition, live released-slot
initialization, source-owned masks, cleared optimizer state, and declared
BatchNorm ownership.

## Core invariance needs two different masks

The structural routing mask and parameter ownership mask serve different
purposes.

For a route indexed as `[source_slot, destination_slot]`, the structural mask
permanently zeros every plastic-to-core edge. Slack, released, and
reinitialized sources are all treated as plastic-side states for this rule.
That preserves the narrow routing property associated with Eqs. 28-29 on PDF
pages 22-23.

The source-owned update mask protects the complete Eq. 2 operator. For each
core source slot, it zeros updates to:

- every incoming weight;
- the incoming bias;
- BatchNorm scale and shift;
- every outgoing route, including routes into slack destinations.

That final row-wide rule is the correction to destination-only ownership. A
core-to-slack outgoing edge belongs to the upstream core operator even though
its destination is plastic. Released slots are also nontrainable. Slack and
properly reinitialized slots are trainable, subject to the separate structural
route mask.

Gradient masking alone is still insufficient when optimizer state already
exists. HOPE-R clears masked momentum and accepts a separate reset mask for
reused entries. Its deterministic momentum plus decoupled-weight-decay step
applies gradient, momentum, and weight decay only where the update mask is one.
Masked values are copied directly from the original parameter tensor, and
their returned momentum is exactly zero. Per-tensor diagnostics report masked
element count, maximum masked drift, maximum masked optimizer state, and the
exact unchanged predicate.

BatchNorm ownership is explicit as well. Scale and shift for channel $i$ are
owned by that channel's stable source slot. Running buffers use one of two
declared policies:

- `frozen`: source and target evaluation select the source track, and target
  adaptation does not update it;
- `dual_track`: source and target own distinct running-mean and
  running-variance tracks, and an update changes only the selected task track.

Dual tracking preserves the source-evaluation map by retaining its source
track. It does not claim that one live set of buffers is simultaneously ideal
for both tasks. It stores task-specific state and must be reported as such.

Finally, evaluation cannot select state implicitly. A `StateDeclaration`
names the task, head, BatchNorm track, stable slot IDs, and slot mask. An
`EvaluationDeclaration` names the dataset, metric, aggregation, checkpoint
rule, and required state. `TaskStateSelector` rejects a task or buffer-track
mismatch. This makes the state restoration and checkpoint semantics exposed
in Parts 10 and 11 part of the result definition rather than hidden setup.

verified_fact (P12-CORE-STATE-INVARIANCE): in the declared fixed-width
fixtures, source-owned update masks plus the declared BatchNorm buffer policy
freeze the complete core operator, including every outgoing route, under
momentum and decoupled weight decay, while the reinitialized slot becomes
gradient-live in two stages.

`deft_transitions.csv` records the partition, lifecycle, gradient, structural
route, complete ownership, optimizer, BatchNorm, and evaluation-state
transitions. The result is a deterministic state-machine witness, not source
retention accuracy.

## The modules compose in one order

HOPE-R is most useful as an ordered contract rather than a bag of independent
patches.

1. Declare the calibration measure, graph, supported block boundaries, and
   task-state policy.
2. Fold finite inference-time BatchNorm state and evaluate all layer neurons
   on the common calibration rows.
3. Build and validate one common Gram, then compute capacities from its
   diagonal and each complete outgoing vector.
4. Enumerate live actions. Score a merge against the executed child sum and an
   eligible block against direct calibrated boundary displacement.
5. Record the current exhaustive scan, live physical payoff, cache storage,
   and calibration work before selecting an action.
6. Resolve the full dependency closure before physical surgery. If graph
   ownership or fan-out is unresolved, stop.
7. Execute the selected supported action, invalidate every returned key, and
   refresh those dependencies before the next scan.
8. At transfer, keep physical widths fixed, partition once by the declared
   layer-wise rule, initialize reusable slots, clear their optimizer state,
   and combine structural routing with complete source-owned update masks.
9. Evaluate only through a declaration that names the task head, slot mask,
   BatchNorm track, metric aggregation, and checkpoint rule.

`design_contract.csv` makes these preconditions, outputs, and fail-closed
boundaries machine-readable. `integration_ablations.csv` records deterministic
controls that isolate repaired module boundaries and their interaction. Those
controls are implementation ablations, not trained-network or accuracy
ablations.

The integration order also exposes a dependency that an isolated equation can
hide. A merge changes physical outgoing and incoming coordinates. That change
invalidates capacities, pair geometry, successor assumptions, and block
scores. A later DEFT partition is meaningful only after those quantities have
been refreshed in the same declared geometry. Likewise, a source accuracy is
meaningful only after its evaluation state has been selected explicitly.

## What the corrected design establishes

The Part 12 claims fall into three evidence classes.

proposed_repair:

- P12-CALIBRATED-COMMON-MEASURE chooses one declared weighted empirical law
  for every neuron in a layer and gives up a strict data-free claim.
- P12-KERNEL-BOUNDARY-CONTRACT makes finite-epsilon folding, zero-scale limits,
  and exact-versus-approximate kernel branches explicit.
- P12-SUM-MAP-MERGE optimizes a realizable physical parent against the
  executed child sum and reports its measured residual.
- P12-DEPENDENCY-CLOSURE invalidates the complete independently enumerated
  cache set for the declared resolved graph contract or fails before surgery.
- P12-LIVE-RESOURCE-ACCOUNTING records live candidates, scans, trajectory,
  cache, refresh, calibration, and physical payoff without a timing claim.
- P12-BLOCK-ELIGIBILITY restricts direct calibrated eviction scoring to the
  implemented identity-shortcut domain.
- P12-FIXED-WIDTH-DEFT specifies stable slots, one partition, reusable-state
  transitions, complete masks, optimizer state, and BatchNorm ownership.

verified_fact:

- P12-COMMON-GRAM-PSD holds on the declared common-measure fixtures and their
  fail-closed spectral validation.
- P12-TWIN-PRESERVATION holds on the declared biased and zero-bias exact-twin
  physical merge fixtures within numerical tolerance.
- P12-REFRESH-EQUIVALENCE holds on the declared branched cache fixture against
  full recomputation.
- P12-CORE-STATE-INVARIANCE holds on the declared fixed-width optimizer,
  buffer, and two-stage gradient fixtures.

independent_inference (P12-GUARANTEE-SCOPE): the integrated fixtures establish
local algebra, geometry, graph, state, and accounting contracts for HOPE-R.
They do not establish trained-network prevalence, optimizer convergence,
final-logit or loss control, accuracy, latency, author-code reproduction, or
universal compression superiority.

That last boundary is not a disclaimer attached after the fact. It is part of
the design. Every result row carries a claim ID and evidence class so a local
fixture cannot silently become a benchmark conclusion.

## What remains unsupported

HOPE-R is not a completed empirical answer to the HOPE research program.

First, the common geometry is calibrated. Its sensitivity to calibration
distribution, sample size, weights, preprocessing, and domain shift is open.
The Part 12 fixtures show algebraic consistency, not population fidelity.

Second, the merge search is finite. Exact twins are anchored, but a general
non-twin pair may leave substantial residual, and a denser direction search
may select a different candidate. Even zero calibration residual does not
guarantee equality outside the calibration rows.

Third, a local residual is not a network guarantee. Later nonlinearities,
normalization, fan-out, and task loss can amplify or attenuate a local change.
No Part 12 test bounds final logits or loss across an arbitrary network.

Fourth, the graph implementation has a deliberately narrow operator domain.
Grouped and depthwise convolution, projection shortcuts, shared weights,
attention, LayerNorm, GroupNorm, non-PH-1 activations, framework tracing, and
unresolved fan-out are unsupported or fail closed.

Fifth, operation and byte counts are not measurements of elapsed time, energy,
or peak device memory. A systems claim requires an implementation on declared
hardware with synchronized measurement and a stated workload.

Sixth, fixed-width DEFT retains task-specific state under dual tracking and
task-state selection. It has not shown that the selected partition is optimal,
that a released slot learns useful target structure, or that source accuracy
is preserved in a trained network.

Finally, this repository does not contain an authenticated author
implementation against which HOPE-R could claim code equivalence. The
paper-literal and proposed branches answer different questions by design.

## The decisive next experiment

A credible empirical evaluation should test the repaired boundaries alone and
together without changing the result definition between methods.

For compression, publish:

- the calibration-row source and weighting rule;
- exact action traces and measured per-action physical residuals;
- results at equal live parameters, FLOPs, and measured latency;
- literal versus common-Gram, literal versus sum-map merge, local versus
  dependency-closure refresh, and internal-score versus direct-block-cost
  controls;
- final-logit, loss, and accuracy changes after each supported action;
- unsupported-action counts and fail-closed reasons.

For transfer, publish:

- the exact layer-wise core counts and stable slot assignments;
- source-owned and structural masks;
- cleared optimizer-state records;
- frozen versus dual-track BatchNorm policy;
- live and restored source-state evaluation separately;
- per-scenario target, source, and H-score records with one aggregation and
  checkpoint rule;
- parameter, optimizer-state, and task-state storage budgets.

The essential ablation is cumulative. A common Gram cannot rescue an
unrealizable physical merge. A better merge cannot rescue stale downstream
caches. Correct cache refresh cannot freeze a core operator whose outgoing row
and BatchNorm buffers remain plastic. Each invariant must survive after the
next module is enabled.

The outcomes of those experiments are unknown. Part 12 supplies the reference
contracts needed to run them without first reopening the specification.

## Reproduction boundary

The canonical Part 12 numerical result contract contains exactly ten files
under `artifacts/part_12/results/`:

- `summary.json`
- `design_contract.csv`
- `common_gram_cases.csv`
- `merge_cases.csv`
- `invalidation_cases.csv`
- `resource_accounting.csv`
- `block_eligibility.csv`
- `deft_transitions.csv`
- `integration_ablations.csv`
- `source_map.csv`

The files contain deterministic local fixtures and evidence metadata. They do
not contain benchmark measurements. The focused tests validate the numerical
contract, and the artifact checksum index authenticates the published files.

Run a disposable independent audit with:

```bash
python3 experiments/audits/part12_corrected_hope/run.py \
  --result-dir artifacts/runs/part_12/manual
```

Run the focused framework-independent module tests with:

```bash
python3 -m unittest \
  tests.test_part12_common_merge \
  tests.test_part12_graph \
  tests.test_part12_deft -v
```

Run the focused audit tests with:

```bash
python -m unittest discover -s experiments/audits/part12_corrected_hope -p 'test_*.py' -v
```

The runner refuses to overwrite a nonempty result directory. These local
fixtures do not turn HOPE-R into author code or reproduce the paper's
CIFAR-100 to SVHN or ImageNet experiments.

The final conclusion is deliberately bounded:

> HOPE's functional-neuron idea survives as a testable reference design when
> geometry, physical realization, graph mutation, resource units, optimizer
> ownership, and evaluation state are all declared. Whether that design wins
> on a trained benchmark remains an experiment, not a consequence of the
> local proofs.
